summary: EarthTwin Explorer is a student-created website that helps users explore Earth locations with environmental and geological features similar to the Moon and Mars. Our project compares terrain, temperature, and other environmental conditions to identify potential Earth analogues for future space exploration. By presenting scientific information through an interactive map and educational pages, we aim to make planetary science more accessible and engaging for students.
details:
EarthTwin Explorer is an educational website designed to identify and compare Earth locations that may serve as analogues for the Moon and Mars.

The website introduces selected analogue locations, including Mauna Kea, Lanzarote, Meteor Crater, the Atacama Desert, McMurdo Dry Valleys, and Holuhraun. It provides information about their geological features and environmental conditions.

The project includes an interactive map, location descriptions, Earth-versus-Mars comparisons, and astronaut exploration missions. Users can explore different locations and learn how studying extreme environments on Earth can help prepare for future lunar and Martian missions.

The website was created using Google Sites. Our goal is to make planetary science easier to understand and encourage students to explore space science through digital technology.
